frozen: 2026-11-06, after round 1 (55774a8a, 223c6ad0) and BEFORE any round-2 fit and before any Broadbalk 1926-1967 grain or straw value was read. Seen from that dataset: README, column names, FYM factor table, notes_data (note 13 quotes one 1930 grain value for strip 14, a fertilized strip that is not a target), and the management columns for strip 3 (cropping by section and year, cultivars, areas) and FYM dates of strip 22. Broadbalk SOC (e-RA 01-BKSOC1843) was read for samples up to 1914 only; the 1936 and later samples were not printed and are not used.
why: Round 1 qualified on memory (Exhaustion Land) but its equilibrium is not credible: continuous unmanured wheat settles at 0.46 t/ha (Broadbalk plot 3 held 0.7-1.0 for a century), bare fallow gives no benefit (Alternate Wheat and Fallow: +0.14 t/ha), and round 1 started Broadbalk at about 66 t C/ha where e-RA estimates 28.8 t C/ha in 1843 (plot 3 then 27.1 in 1865, 24.2 in 1914; plot 2.2 50.7 in 1865 and 71.2 in 1914).

model_changes.initial_state: Rothamsted sites spin up to measured soil carbon with no prior manure: Broadbalk to 28.8 t C/ha total in 1843 (e-RA 01-BKSOC1843 estimate), Exhaustion Land (Hoosfield) to 33.8 t C/ha in 1852 (RothC description, Hoosfield); the prior plant input is scaled until active C + IOM (Falloon et al. 1998) equals the target. Woburn keeps the 1.70 t C/ha/yr prior input plus a fitted prior manure M0_w (its history before 1876 is unknown).
model_changes.n_input: I(t) = F + W(t). W(t) is Rothamsted's measured wet deposition (Goulding et al. 1998, New Phytologist 139: nitrate + ammonium N in precipitation 1 + 3 kg N/ha/yr in 1855 rising to 8 + 10 in 1980): 4 kg before 1855, linear to 18 kg in 1980. F (free-living fixation, seed and dry deposition, held constant) is fitted. For AD 200, W and the industrial part of F do not apply (pre-industrial deposition about 0.5 kg N/ha/yr or less, Dentener et al. 2006); that value is a stated scenario, not fitted.
model_changes.uptake: Crops take up N in every vegetated month (winter wheat October-July, spring barley and oats April-July, potatoes May-September) at r_u x min(1, max(0, T)/10), T the month's mean temperature (uptake follows thermal growth). Replaces the fixed spring windows.
model_changes.manure: Fitted FYM humified share h_fym (RothC default 0.02, bounds 0.02-0.6), the rest split equally DPM/RPM. Motivated by the documented RothC miss on Hoosfield's plot manured only 1852-71 and round 1's too-short manure memory.
model_changes.clover: Red clover residues revised to the literature on cut forage swards: 0.8 t C/ha/yr at C:N 20 in each clover year and 2.0 t C/ha at C:N 19 (about 105 kg N in roots and stubble) when ploughed in. Round 1 used 1.5 t C at C:N 15 yearly and 2.0 at C:N 15.
model_changes.unchanged: RothC-26.3 pools and rate factors, the evaporation amendment, SUNDIAL C:N 8.5, grain N 23 kg/t, residue C line, residue C:N 40, Burns leaching, climate potential kappa x A0.

development.data: all spent: Broadbalk raw per-plot yields 1879-1925 for plot 3, plot 2/2.2 and plot 2.1 (FYM since 1885, nil before); Broadbalk SOC 1865-1914 for plots 3, 2.2, 2.1; Woburn wheat and barley per plot 1879-1926 for plots 1, 7, 10a, 11a, 11b with their full treatment histories; Exhaustion Land cereals 1902-1922 and 1935, plots 1-10; the Alternate Wheat and Fallow aggregate (wheat after one-year fallow vs Broadbalk plot 3: +0.6 t/ha in the first 10 years from 1856, +0.14 over the next 60), modelled as an alternate wheat-fallow plot on the Broadbalk start state compared with the modelled plot 3.
development.objective: mean over five evidence groups (Broadbalk yields, Woburn yields, Exhaustion Land yields, Broadbalk SOC, wheat-fallow aggregate) of the mean over the group's series of the mean squared natural-log error (yields floored at 0.05 t/ha; the wheat-fallow terms as ln of modelled (wheat-fallow / continuous) against ln((Y3 + delta) / Y3) with Y3 the observed plot-3 mean of the period).
development.parameters: F 0-60 kg N/ha/yr, r_u 0.05-0.9, kappa 1-5, h_fym 0.02-0.6, M0_w 0-3 t C/ha/yr; differential evolution, seed 20261106.
development.selection: output/soil_fertility_round2_20261106/selection.json with producer hashes, committed before the evaluation.

evaluation.data: Broadbalk Wheat 1926-1967 (10.23637/rbk1-yld2667-01, CC BY 4.0), strips 3 (nil), 21 (FYM since 1885) and 22 (FYM since 1843), every section, wheat years. Each strip x section plot runs from 1843 with its strip's history and, from 1926, its section's recorded cropping (fallow years: no crop, no manure). Weather: Rothamsted observed. Same field as development (temporal holdout of the same strips 1-42 years later), declared.

metrics.T1_level: strip 3, all wheat plot-years: MAE log10 against A0's (existing response) and mean log10 bias of the model.
metrics.T2_manure: strips 21 and 22 against strip 3 in the same section and year: log10 ratio; model against the null 0; MAE and Pearson r.
metrics.T3_fallow: strip 3, each year: log10(first wheat after a fallow / mean of the strip's wheat in sections whose last fallow was 2 or more years earlier); model against the null 0. Strips 21 and 22 reported. Confound declared: fallowing also controlled weeds (herbicides from 1957 on section IA, 1963 on VB, 1964 on all but VA), which the model does not represent.

evaluation.qualify_if: T1: MAE <= A0's and |mean log10 bias| <= 0.10. T2: MAE <= 0.95 x null's and r > 0. T3: predicted mean > 0 and MAE <= 0.95 x null's. All three.
evaluation.reported: the round-1 selection on the same targets; nitrogen-fertilized strips (N response) as a secondary diagnostic.

consequence: No production change from this test. If it qualifies, the next declared step designs the integration: yield per sown hectare under fallow, manure and legume regimes with an AD 200 N-input scenario, feeding the shared grain -> residents -> reach chain. If it fails, the failure is recorded and the capacity layer stays as it is.
scripts: harvest/soil_fertility.py and scripts/soil_fertility_common.py (round-2 options default to round-1 behaviour), scripts/soil_fertility_round2.py (fit, selection, evaluation)
